body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Comment says a following off waits on the queue, but the off path runs synchronously (confidence high)**

The comment says the turn-on goes on the queue "so an off that follows waits for this camera to open and releases it". The off branch (lines 924-934) never touches `queue`, though. It calls `handle.turnWebcamOff()` right away. That call bumps `cameraRequest` (recorder-engine.ts:772), and the in-flight `turnWebcamOn` sees it has been superseded and stops the camera it opened (recorder-engine.ts:790-792, 810). So the behaviour is correct, but the comment describes a mechanism that does not exist. The only thing the queue orders is one turn-on after another. Reword it to say that: a later turn-on waits for this one, and a turn-off supersedes it through the engine's request counter.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Gap segments get random ids, so a take with gaps never reuses its Share export (confidence medium)**

This test checks that the seeded gap segments get distinct ids, and `gapSegments` creates them with `crypto.randomUUID()` (webcam-model.ts:155). Share builds its fingerprint from that seeded layer: `initialScene(...)` → `seedWebcamScene` (scene.ts:140), then `wholeFingerprint(scene.webcam)` (share-recording.tsx:126-130). The fingerprint hashes `stableStringify(webcam)`, which is the whole layer including the segment ids (export-reuse.ts:81-83). The existing tests assume that seeding the same sidecar twice gives the same fingerprint (export-reuse.test.ts:176, share-recording.test.tsx:154). For a take with `gaps` that is no longer true: each mount, and each new `probe.durationSec`, produces a new fingerprint. A second Share then never matches the earlier export and re-encodes the whole recording. Nothing tells the user why.

Suggested fix: derive the ids of seeded gap segments from the gap itself (for example `gap-${startMs}`). Then add a test here that seeds the same `withGaps(...)` twice and gets the same `wholeFingerprint`.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: The 'cut camera frame is dropped and closed' path is never exercised (confidence high)**

The comment says a frame the old camera still delivers after `cut()` is "dropped (and closed), not relayed". But `cut()` cancels the reader (webcam-relay.ts:66-70), which closes the fake stream, so `first.push(late)` throws inside the `try` and the frame never reaches the pump. The branch at webcam-relay.ts:91-93 (`current !== reader` → `value.close()`) never runs. The test also never asserts `late.close`. A frame read before the cut and delivered after it would leak a `VideoFrame` if that branch broke, and this test would still pass. To cover it, enqueue the late frame before calling `cut()` (or don't close the stream on cancel), then assert `late.close` was called.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: 'At the camera's rate' test can't tell the camera's rate from the fallback (confidence high)**

The stubbed camera reports `frameRate: 30` (line 1620), and the fallback in recorder-engine.ts:709 is `WEBCAM_FPS`, which is also 30 (webcam-track.ts:19). `toEqual({ frameRate: 30 })` therefore passes whether the engine reads `getSettings().frameRate` or ignores it. To make the test pin what its name says, give the stub another rate (say 24) and expect that value.

<!-- wachi:finding -->
